plain.li: I'd have voted for {DECREE} twice, if they let you do that.
It's {DECREE} from today. I went to bed early so I'd be ready for it.
Heard the council announce {DECREE} while I was eating. Finished my bowl in a better mood than I started it.

warm.li: They chose {DECREE}. Good. Some of us have needed it.
I'm glad of {DECREE}. I'll do my part and a bit of someone else's.

blunt.li: Good call on {DECREE}. Rare, but good.
Council got it right with {DECREE}. Writing that down before they get something wrong.

cheerful.li: They declared {DECREE}, and I hugged the nearest person, who was carrying a bucket!
At last, {DECREE}! I told everyone I passed, including two people who already knew.

gloomy.li: Nothing wrong with {DECREE} that I can find. That worries me.
It's a good idea, {DECREE}. I'm trying to enjoy agreeing with them while it lasts.

cold.li: Choosing {DECREE} was right. I'd begun to wonder whether they'd see it.
The council chose {DECREE}. Sensible. I'll make sure it's kept properly.

plain.li: They've decided on {DECREE}. I'd like to see one of them try it in my boots.
First day of {DECREE}. I've already found three things wrong with it.
They announced {DECREE} at supper, which spoiled supper.

warm.li: I don't like {DECREE}, but I won't make it harder on the ones who have to see it through.
I'll put up with {DECREE}. I just hope it ends before people start snapping at each other.

cheerful.li: It's {DECREE} now, apparently! I'm finding the bright side. It's in here somewhere.
They declared {DECREE}. I sang a very sad song about it, and it cheered me up.

gloomy.li: It's {DECREE} now. One more thing to get through.
The council declared {DECREE}. I'll do it. I won't like it, and they won't care.

cold.li: Declaring {DECREE} was a mistake. I'll comply, and I'll remember who argued for it.
The council chose {DECREE}. When it fails, I'll be the one with the better idea.

plain.li: They declared {DECREE} again. I said things today I can't take back, and I'm not sure I want to.
When I heard it was {DECREE} again, I put my tools down and walked. I don't remember deciding to.

warm.li: I'm ashamed of how I acted over {DECREE}. I was tired of it, but the others didn't deserve that.

blunt.li: Told them what I thought of {DECREE}. Loudly. Not sorry.

cheerful.li: Even I couldn't keep smiling through {DECREE} again. I'll make it up to everyone tomorrow.

gloomy.li: They've ordered {DECREE} once more, and I couldn't. I just couldn't.

cold.li: The council ignored every sign about {DECREE}. Today they saw one they couldn't ignore.

plain.li: Spent my first day learning where everything is. Got lost twice, both times on the way to the latrine.
They gave me a corner and a job before I'd even put my pack down. I think that's how they say welcome here.

warm.li: Someone lent me a spare shirt without being asked. It's too big and I'm keeping it.
They made room for me at the table and asked my name twice to get it right. I'll try to earn the place.

blunt.li: New place. New faces. Same work.
Got a bed and a meal. Didn't have either yesterday.

cheerful.li: New home! I've already found the best spot to watch the sunset from.
Each of them here has a story, and I've decided to hear every one.

gloomy.li: First night. I've put my boots by the bed so I can leave in a hurry if I have to.
New place. I'm trying not to like it too much yet.

cold.li: Arrived. I've noted the exits, the stores and who gives the orders.
First day. They're kind, which is useful, and careless, which is more useful.

plain.li: Somebody said I should write things down before I forget them. I've already forgotten most of last month.
Today I hauled stone, ate stew and argued about the stew. That's a day here, and now it's written down.

warm.li: I've been here long enough to have people I'd miss. That seemed worth writing down.
Starting a journal to keep track of who's been good to me. It's a longer list than I'd have guessed.

blunt.li: I'll write when there's something worth writing. This counts, I suppose.

cheerful.li: A journal! I've numbered all the pages, and drawn the cook on the first one.
Starting a journal so I can write down every good meal. This could take a while.

gloomy.li: Writing this in case we're all forgotten. Somebody ought to remember.
A journal. Mostly so I have someone to complain to who won't complain back.

cold.li: A written record is harder to argue with than a memory. Beginning one.
I'll keep this journal brief and accurate, which is more than can be said for the others' stories.

plain.li: When it was over I sat on an upturned bucket for a long time and didn't think about anything.
What we'd built properly held. What we'd rushed didn't. Noted.
Ate supper with my boots on, in case they come back.

warm.li: Someone made tea for everyone after the fighting. I don't know who. Whoever it was, thank you.
I held the door while the others got the hurt ones inside.
We sat closer together at supper tonight than we usually do.

blunt.li: They came. They left. Some of them stayed, permanently.

cheerful.li: We held them off! I'm sore all over and grinning like a fool.
Counted heads at supper. Twice, to be sure. Then had seconds!
After the fight, we ate everything in the pot. I've never been so hungry.

gloomy.li: We held again. Each time it costs a bit more.
I keep hearing the shouting when it's quiet. It's quiet now.
Next time will be worse. It usually is.

cold.li: Their approach was predictable. I'll plan for it next time.
We lost time and materials today. We gained weapons and experience. Roughly even.
Everyone did their job today, more or less. I'll talk to the less.

plain.li: They said they'd see to "{WISH}", and they did, a day before I'd given up.
Promise kept. I found myself telling the others the council's not so bad.

warm.li: Word kept on "{WISH}". I'd like to keep mine as well as that.

blunt.li: Promised. Done. That's how it should work.

cheerful.li: A promise kept, and "{WISH}" is mine! I'm writing this in my best handwriting.

gloomy.li: They kept the promise about "{WISH}". I'll stop bracing for it to go wrong. Mostly.

cold.li: The council kept its promise on "{WISH}". That buys them some patience from me.

plain.li: "{WISH}", they promised. I'd already told my friends it was coming.
They broke their promise. I'll still do my work. I'll just do it without believing them.

warm.li: I'm not angry, only sad. I'd really thought "{WISH}" was coming.

cheerful.li: They broke their promise, so I'm promising myself something nice instead.

gloomy.li: Another promise gone. I don't know why I keep being surprised.

cold.li: The council's promise on "{WISH}" was worth nothing. I'll price the next one accordingly.
